content.value_statement: Apple app teams need clear choices for charts, images, collections, web content, and sharing. This skill maps content needs to Apple HIG components.
actual_capabilities: Recommends Apple content components for charts, collections, image display, web content, sharing, color selection, and tvOS lockups.
Explains when to use Swift Charts, UICollectionView, WKWebView, UIActivityViewController, image views, image wells, and color wells.
Summarizes accessibility expectations for charts, images, collections, web views, activity views, and focusable lockups.
Provides platform notes for iOS, iPadOS, macOS, tvOS, watchOS, and visionOS where the references include them.
Flags common HIG mistakes, including duplicate share actions, browser-like web views, unclear chart color use, and unstable collection layouts.
limitations: It covers content display components, not full app architecture, navigation, visual branding, or production code review.
It is based on included reference snapshots and may not reflect later Apple documentation changes.
It can guide implementation choices, but it does not compile, test, or certify Apple platform code.
It depends on the user to provide platform targets, content type, data size, and accessibility requirements.

use_cases.title: Choose a Component
use_cases.description: A designer compares charts, collections, image views, web views, and activity views for a new Apple app screen.

use_cases.title: Review Data Display
use_cases.description: An iOS engineer checks chart hierarchy, axes, labels, color use, interaction, and VoiceOver support before implementation.

use_cases.title: Plan Platform Behavior
use_cases.description: A product lead validates which content patterns work across iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple TV, Apple Watch, and visionOS.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Content Component
prompt_templates.prompt: I am building an Apple app screen for [content type] on [platforms]. Recommend the right HIG content component and explain the tradeoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Improve a Chart Design
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this chart concept for an Apple app: [chart purpose, data type, user task]. Give HIG guidance for marks, axes, labels, color, and accessibility.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Collection Experience
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a collection view for [item type] with [item count] items on [platforms]. Cover layout, selection, reordering, empty states, and accessibility.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Cross-Platform Screen
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this screen spec against Apple HIG content component guidance: [screen spec]. Identify component choices, platform issues, accessibility gaps, and recommended changes.

output_examples.input: I need to show monthly step counts in an iPhone health app.
output_examples.output: Use Swift Charts with bars for monthly totals. Keep the lower axis bound meaningful, summarize the main trend, and support VoiceOver labels or Audio Graphs.

output_examples.input: Should a recipe app use a web view for external cooking articles?
output_examples.output: Use a web view only for brief embedded content. For broader browsing, prefer Safari-related flows and provide forward and back controls when multi-page navigation is expected.

output_examples.input: How should I present a library of movie posters on Apple TV?
output_examples.output: Use tvOS lockups or posters with consistent sizing, enough spacing for focus expansion, and clear labels for each focused item.

best_practices: Provide the content type, primary task, target platforms, data size, and whether content changes over time.
Ask for accessibility guidance with every recommendation, especially for charts, images, web content, and focusable collections.
Use the skill early to choose components, then verify final details against current Apple documentation.
anti_patterns: Requesting a component choice without saying whether the content is data, media, web content, or a collection.
Using web views as full browser replacements or charts that require interaction to reveal critical information.
Ignoring platform support limits, such as lockups on non-tvOS platforms or activity views outside supported contexts.

faq.question: What components does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers charts, collection views, image views, web views, activity views, lockups, color wells, and image wells.

faq.question: Can it generate SwiftUI or UIKit code?
faq.answer: It can guide component choice and configuration. Ask separately for implementation code after the design direction is clear.

faq.question: Does it replace Apple Human Interface Guidelines?
faq.answer: No. It summarizes included HIG references and should be checked against current Apple documentation for final decisions.

faq.question: Is it useful for accessibility reviews?
faq.answer: Yes. It highlights VoiceOver, audio graph, alt text, focus order, target size, and color differentiation concerns.

faq.question: Which platforms are covered?
faq.answer: It covers platform notes present in the included references for iOS, iPadOS, macOS, tvOS, watchOS, and visionOS.

faq.question: When should I use another HIG skill?
faq.answer: Use foundation, layout, pattern, or platform skills when the question is mainly about color, typography, navigation, layout, or platform behavior.
